correctness.rationale: Exact per-petal private-path and middle-set independence statistics establish a simplicial map. The six local filtered complexes are respectively empty units, two-point sets, an edge, a path, and a simplex; each restriction is a homotopy equivalence. Joins and all finite intersections of the threshold covers inherit these equivalences; finite-subcomplex-cover gluing and the hub-star pushout give the global map equivalence for every m,k. The independent quadrilateral-bouquet Morse model has one zero-cell and binomial(m,k-1) cells in dimension 2k-3, with global acyclicity proven by a monotone hub/middle/endpoint ordering. Tested all 16 finite pairs with independent mod-2 boundary ranks; integrality comes from homotopy proof, not numerical rank.

value.rationale: The contraction theorem transfers an all-threshold sphere-wedge classification to an infinite nonbipartite family, including the natural first nontrivial higher-threshold case (m,k)=(3,4) and all k>=4. A graph-edge contraction is not generically a robust-clique homotopy equivalence, and the proof identifies a genuine local double-filtration condition that makes this family stable. This supplies a structural technique beyond routine enumeration or a change of notation.
